newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Ciampi optimistic recovery has begun.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Ciampi optimistic recovery has begun.

text.p: Italian Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said on Tuesday he saw "good reason" to believe economic recovery was now underway.

"There are good reasons to believe that the economy is now in recovery," Ciampi told the Senate (upper house) ahead of a final vote on the government's three-year programme of economic targets for 1998-2000, known as the DPEF.
Ciampi cited "reasons of closeness to the other large economies of the continent, which all expect rates of growth higher than two percent next year."
The DPEF targets two percent real GDP growth in 1998 and a deficit-GDP ratio of 2.8 percent after 25 trillion lire of deficit cuts in the 1998 budget. Ciampi said.

"Next year...the public budget will be at least neutral for the economy, the international environment will be more favourable to growth and interest rates will, we hope, be lower than today. The discount rate is currently at 6.75 percent.
"I therefore believe that the forecast of a two percent rise in GDP is justified," Ciampi said.
